issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem thm:shock_interaction cites Theorem thm:more_general_case as covering it. However, thm:more_general_case assumes the shock hypersurfaces lie in the open space-time domain Ω_T = Ω×(0,T). The interaction in thm:shock_interaction occurs at the terminal time T, which is on the boundary and not contained in Ω_T. Hence the cited theorem does not apply, and no independent proof is supplied.

failure_location.quote: A complete argument is contained in the proof of the more general higher-dimensional interaction result, Theorem~\ref{thm:more_general_case}; the present statement is a special case of that theorem.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a separate proof for terminal-time interactions or extend Theorem thm:more_general_case to allow intersections on the boundary t=T, including the necessary local boundary analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence rate for terminal-time shock interactions is unsupported, and the main 1D theorem, which relies on shock interaction analysis, is not fully established.
issues.title: Invalid reduction of terminal-time shock interaction to interior multidimensional theorem

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:compound_wave asserts a convergence rate for compound waves but provides no proof. A compound wave combines shock and rarefaction features and the stated rate is different from the pure shock and pure rarefaction results, so the omitted proof is a nontrivial missing argument. The main 1D theorem later relies on this result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists an index \(j\in\{1,\dots,M\}\) such that \int_{\Lambda_j} \left| \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F}(u_{\theta^*}) \right|\, \d \z \leq \frac{C}{M}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs the integral of |∇·F(uθ*)| over the transition region Ω_i to be O(h^{1/2}). The only global control from the loss is ∫_{Ω_T}|∇·F(uθ*)| ≲ 1, which does not imply such a local bound for an arbitrary region of measure O(h^{1/2}). In the 1D proof, this was achieved by a strip-selection argument over M=h^{-1/2} disjoint strips. The multidimensional proof asserts the bound without constructing or selecting the strips.
